RQ1.rationale: Directly addresses general CubeSat/nanosatellite mission/system modeling through a reusable SysML reference model, though EPS is only a secondary/past-phase element.

RQ2.rationale: Claims integrability, reproducibility/distribution, reuse, consistency, traceability, and effort-reduction outcomes, but evidence is mostly conceptual and not EPS reliability-focused.

RQ3.rationale: No EPS-specific verification procedure integrated into the model before physical development is reported.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper is part of the INCOSE SSWG MBSE Challenge CubeSat reference-model lineage, summarizing FireSat, RAX Phase 1, RAX behavior/power/communications Phase 2, Phase 3 enterprise/trade-study work, and current Phase 4 reference-model distribution. Prior-phase evidence should not be double counted as independent unless earlier papers are separately extracted.
bibliographic_review_management.bibliographic_data_quality_note: Prompt metadata and markdown title page disagree on title/authors; both are retained for auditability.

study_context_population.mission_platform: Generic CubeSat/CubeSat Enterprise reference model; RAX three-unit CubeSat and hypothetical FireSat are lineage examples.
study_context_population.size_form_factor: CubeSat standardized unit cube of 10 cm on a side and about 1 kg per cube; typically one to three units, with some up to six units; RAX is described as a three-unit CubeSat.
study_context_population.mission_name: CubeSat Reference Model; prior examples include Radio Aurora Explorer (RAX) and hypothetical FireSat.
study_context_population.mission_domain: CubeSat space systems including space segment, ground segment, launch/deployment services, external environment, external constraints/regulations, and mission operations.
study_context_population.organization_type: INCOSE Space Systems Working Group Challenge Team spanning students, professors, engineers, software developers, government, industry, academia, and modeling/simulation tool providers.
study_context_population.project_maturity: Interim/current phase: logical reference model down to subsystem level, stakeholder and requirements structure, Cal Poly requirements model, and distribution plans; detailed refinement, correctness verification, and release remain future work.

mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.stated_objective_pain_point: Develop and distribute a CubeSat SysML reference model that captures basic CubeSat project features, provides a framework/checklist for future CubeSat developers, reduces small-team systems-engineering burden, and promotes uniformity and consistency.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Generic logical CubeSat Enterprise architecture including CubeSat Space System, CubeSat Ground System, stakeholders, external environment/constraints, and provided services. RQ1: Generic CubeSat missions can be modeled as a SysML/OOSEM reference model with stakeholders, needs, objectives, constraints, measures, requirements, use cases, domain/enterprise boundaries, lifecycle/operations phases, and logical space/ground subsystem architectures.
The approach addresses limited early knowledge by giving reusable logical elements and a general decomposition that can be tailored to mission-specific physical architectures.
EPS contribution is secondary: the paper summarizes prior power-subsystem behavior and energy trade studies rather than developing a full EPS reference model.
RQ2: Claimed MBSE outcomes include integrability, automatic consistency across views, generated documentation, traceability, reuse, checklist support, uniformity, lifecycle continuity, reproducibility through distribution, and reduced SE burden for small teams.
Evidence is mostly conceptual; the strongest reported evidence is prior RAX application and executable/trade-study demonstrations for power/communications variables.
No measured reliability, integration failure reduction, reproducibility adoption metric, or cost/schedule/effort baseline is reported.
RQ3: No EPS-specific verification procedure is integrated or demonstrated before physical development.

Generic V&V support appears through MBSE definition, Cal Poly testing requirements, tester stakeholder roles, traceability, pre-launch integration/test lifecycle coverage, and planned model-correctness verification.

Future plans include model-element refinement, correctness verification, copyright/licensing work, and distribution release planning.
The model distribution process is under development.

direct_evidence_quotes_supporting_classi.quote: Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) is the formalized application of modeling to support system requirements, design, analysis, verification and validation activities beginning in the conceptual design phase and continuing throughout development and later life cycle phases.
At the core of MBSE is the development of the system model that helps integrate other discipline-specific engineering models and simulations.
The project's application of MBSE uses the Systems Modeling Language (SysML) and graphical modeling tools from No Magic.
These logical elements can be reused for specifying a mission specific CubeSat.
The reference model can support all life cycle stages for a CubeSat mission.
The model also supports all phases of operations: pre-launch integration and test, launch, early orbit checkout, and full mission operations.

Two trade studies were demonstrated: 1) On-board energy level as a function of solar panel area and maximum battery capacity and 2) quantity of data downlinked as a function of orbital altitude and ground station network.
In addition to the model file, the distribution will include video recordings that explain and walk through the model and its components.
The future plans include: (i) refining the CubeSat Reference Model to include additional details for each of the model elements, (ii) verifying the correctness of the model

MBSE holds the promise of reducing the burden of systems engineering tasks, which is beneficial to small CubeSat teams, and a properly designed reference model can serve as a checklist to these teams and promote uniformity and consistency across future CubeSat models.
